findings.requirement: REQ-112 (criterion 1, description «The port», О17); REQ-111 (criterion 11, files list, guard row (8))
findings.point: а (criteria compatible only through an unnamed change, AP-016); б (the lesson of decisions/0045 item 2)
findings.where: REQ-112 criterion 1: «each with a 40-character commit sha … `git show <sha>:<path>` of each equals the current original byte for byte»; REQ-111 criterion 11: «gh run list --workflow app.yml --branch <that branch> … → success on that sha»; REQ-111 files list: «.github/workflows/app.yml (changed: the job e2e, the paths, one docker step)».
findings.problem: app/test/unit/port-parity.test.js runs in `npm run check` of the job `check` of .github/workflows/app.yml, whose actions/checkout step has only `persist-credentials: false`, so the default history depth of one commit applies (check.yml, by contrast, has `fetch-depth: 0`, decisions/0045 item 2, fact Ф9: without the history handoffs-check is red on GitHub). Measured: a `git clone --depth 1` of base/M1SITE-20261119-01 holds one commit; `git cat-file -t b5df4a808243a1f669ad3697374c265c720a7c31` there → «could not get object info»; `git show b5df4a8…:tools/src/pixel-office/public/layout.js` → exit 128; in the full repository the same command equals the original byte for byte. A port header can never name the pushed commit itself, so criterion 1 is red in app.yml and REQ-111 criterion 11 cannot pass. Neither block names a change of the checkout (the files list names three changes of app.yml, guard row (8) names the rows of ci-workflow.test.js), and the RELEASE-VALIDATOR step of criterion 11 («removes every path that is not in the list») does not say that .git stays.
findings.fix: Name how the parity oracle gets the originals in CI: either the job check of app.yml with the full history (in the files list of REQ-111, in guard row (8) — ci-workflow.test.js does not pin checkout options today, so say whether a rule and a damaged copy are added — and in REQ-112's description of the port), or an oracle that needs no git history (for example a recorded hash of each original that the test compares, keeping «a change of an original makes the test red»). Say that the path-removal check of criterion 11 keeps .git.

findings.point: б and д (the owner gate G9 against the text of a criterion)
findings.where: Description: «The function entry answers the demo questionnaire only in the public languages.» Criterion 7: «`?lang=kk` → Kazakh through the local server and Russian through the function entry» (said for GET questionnaire only); «`POST /api/demo/result?lang=<l>` with the JSON body … → 200 and the result in that language», tested «through the app of the local server and through the function entry».
findings.problem: No public-language rule is written for the result route. Read as written, criterion 7 asks the function entry to answer `POST /api/demo/result?lang=kk` in Kazakh — the kk strings of the intake (solution names, summaries, not_suitable_when, no_match_text) served on the production URL to anyone who asks — while G9's default holds («kk built and tested, hidden on production»; PLAN NEVER-DO 14: never show kk publicly without the gate). No row of the block would catch it: criterion 8 checks kk through the local server only, criterion 12 serves the public set through createApp, the post-deploy record sends the result request without lang, and criterion 9 (g) ties the build's languages to «the languages of the function entry in criterion 7», which name only the questionnaire.
findings.fix: Write the language rule of the function entry for both demo routes (kk and an unknown value → Russian, as for the questionnaire), with test rows in criterion 7 for `POST /api/demo/result?lang=kk` (and an unknown value) through the function entry, and let criterion 9 (g) cover the languages of both routes.

findings.point: а (two criteria that cannot hold together under the plain reading, AP-016)
findings.where: Criterion 10: «a script outside the project that reads the sample's data.js as text — every string value of its kk block and the second argument of every `L(…)` call that has three or more words — finds none of them verbatim in the texts module or the intake»; criterion 2: the kk theme positions exactly «Авто», «Ашық», «Қараңғы» (decisions/0084 §3 item 15).
findings.problem: The limit «that has three or more words» stands after the L(…) clause only, so the plain reading compares every string value of the kk block. Measured on docs/design/samples/picker-v3-approved-2026-10-26/data.js: the kk block (lines 50-90) has 114 string values, 74 of them under three words, among them `th_auto: 'Авто'`, `you: 'Сіз'`, 'Артқа', 'Білмеймін', 'Дайын', 'Жабу'. Criterion 2 requires the kk value «Авто», so under that reading criterion 10 is red on every correct build. «verbatim in the texts module» also does not say whether an equal whole value or a part of a value counts (a part would hit 'Сіз' inside ordinary kk sentences). The author's own trial compared only strings of three or more words (144 of them), so the text and its trial disagree.
findings.fix: State the word limit for both sets of strings, how words are counted, and whether a hit is an equal whole value or a part of one, so that the script cannot hit words that criterion 2 or the scene's kk keys require; keep the printed count above zero.

findings.point: а (a promise of the plan with no check of its content); PLAN §4.2 (seeds are not weakened)
findings.where: PLAN M1 «Owner sees»: «a one-tap demo survey (5 questions; the result says which kind of product Sai builds and what it cannot build yet, and offers «Описать идею»)»; REQ-111 description (the same words); criterion 5 «every solution has at least one not_suitable_when text»; criterion 12 «the result shows the name of a solution or the no-match text, the not_suitable_when texts and «Описать идею»».
findings.problem: «Which kind of product» is checked (the closed list of six solution ids, one per kind of PLAN §2), but «what it cannot build yet» is checked only as the presence of not_suitable_when texts, whose content is free (the format allows any text of 1-150 signs), so a result that says nothing about what Sai cannot build in V1 passes every criterion. The look description puts PLAN §2's «does not build» list into block D of the landing, local only under G8 «б» (docs/design/V1-public-look.md 8.1 D), maps «what Sai does not build yet» on the result to `not_suitable_when` (7.14), and shows no lists on the no-match result (7.12). So on production no tested text says what Sai cannot build yet; the reader test of criterion 14 allows one wrong answer of twelve.
findings.fix: Add a check with its test that the demo result — for every recommended solution and for the no-match case — says what Sai cannot build yet in V1, against a closed list taken from PLAN §2 «What they do not build in V1» (for example texts the design names, tested in every language, and seen on the result screen by the e2e of criterion 12).

findings.requirement: REQ-111 (description «Words used» and «The production build…», criterion 9, open question О3)
findings.point: б (ARCH §19.3; decisions/0091 item 8: a change of ARCH is a dated row citing a decision)
findings.where: «The public languages: ru and en while G9 holds its default, one constant of the source whose place the design names (ARCH §17 PUBLIC_LANGS)»; «Changing G8 or G9 is a release that changes the one constant of each»; criterion 9 (b), (c): the build removes every kk value from the public set.
findings.problem: ARCH §19.3: «Values that must change without a redeploy — test_mode, registration_mode, public_langs, the kill switch — live in platform_settings (admin + re-auth)». The block makes the public languages a source constant and strips kk from the public set at build, so kk can be shown only by a release, and a later platform_settings value public_langs could not take effect for the static texts. The block cites ARCH §17 but not §19.3, question О3 does not name the conflict, and PROGRESS «Plan amendments» has no row for it (decisions/0116 О26 recorded the earlier departures from ARCH this way). CLAUDE.md: a disagreement is not resolved silently.
findings.fix: Name the departure from ARCH §19.3 and its reason in the description (no admin before M2, the demo reads no database, the static public set cannot read platform_settings) and put it into the open questions with its default, so ORCH records it in decisions/0123 with a «Plan amendments» row — or choose a form that §19.3 allows.

findings.point: а (a reading that contradicts the approved sample and the look description; AP-055)
findings.where: Criterion 6: «at 320×568 the canvas fits the width with no horizontal scroll».
findings.problem: In the approved sample the office canvas is wider than a narrow window and the stage pans with a camera (office.js lines 476-486). The look description measured it: the canvas CSS width is 700 px at 390×844 and at 320×568 (Rw = max(W, 350)), «the stage clips the wider canvas (overflow: hidden)», with a camera offset of 155 or 190 logical px on question 5 (docs/design/V1-public-look.md 9.1, 9.14, 12). Read literally, «the canvas fits the width» is false for that page, so the stage test turns red on a page that follows the sample, or the page leaves the look the owner approved (decision 0083; WF-04).
findings.fix: Say what is measured at 320×568 in a way that agrees with the look description — for example no horizontal scroll of the page and the visible stage box within the window, with the canvas allowed to be wider inside the clipping stage — or decide the opposite and have the look gate 03b change the description; one reading in both documents.

findings.where: «every fillStyle is a value of the palette it was given or a scene constant the design lists (seven distinct #rrggbb values are all found back …); a palette value that is not #rrggbb is replaced by a neutral constant with no exception».
findings.problem: «seven» has no source: the look description's scene reads 18 scene colour tokens and four page tokens (6.2, 9.1); it also lists `--sc-dim-alpha`, a number that the #rrggbb rule would replace, and alpha fills derived from `--sc-dim` (9.11) that are neither palette values nor listed constants once the test passes marker colours.
findings.fix: Say which palette the test passes (the scene tokens the look names), that every given value is found back, and how alpha fills are listed (constants per theme, or palette entries); settle it together with the look gate 03b.

findings.point: б (bookkeeping of departures from ARCH and PLAN, decisions/0091 item 8)
findings.where: Criterion 11 and О10 («the runner's Chrome»); guard row (8) (new paths of app.yml); criterion 8 and О9 (demo-parity at the int level).
findings.problem: ARCH §3 and §18 say «Chromium in CI» for the e2e job; ARCH §18's paths list of app.yml gains tools/src/picker/**, tools/src/node-floor.js and the two office originals; PLAN M1.4 lists demo-parity among the unit tests. None changes an outcome of a check, but none is named for a «Plan amendments» row.
findings.fix: List them for decision 0123 (an open question or a sentence of the description), so ORCH writes the rows, as decisions/0116 О26 did.

findings.requirement: REQ-111 (criterion 10, the CSP paragraph of the description); REQ-112 (criterion 9)
findings.point: а (AP-120 borders; AP-094 a «none» without the whole set)
findings.where: Criterion 10 bans `eval(`, `new Function`, `document.write` and `Math.random`; REQ-112 criterion 9: «no file of app/public/office names fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon or a /api address»; the description: «the code sets no style attribute and no HTML from a string».
findings.problem: Criterion 10 names no identifier borders and no benign twin for these forms (AP-120's own example is `eval(` inside `retrieval(`; only outerHTML has the twin `outerHTMLx`); REQ-112 criterion 9 lacks «as a whole identifier», which its criterion 3 has, so `prefetch` or `fetchedAt` would be hit as substrings. The list of HTML-from-string sinks (innerHTML of REQ-109, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write) leaves out `createContextualFragment`, `DOMParser` `parseFromString`, `setHTMLUnsafe` and `srcdoc`, while the description says «no HTML from a string».
findings.fix: Name the borders and one benign twin for each code form; add the other HTML-from-string sinks or narrow the sentence to the listed forms.

findings.point: а (literal forms that the check's own formatter rewrites)
findings.where: «has `<html lang="ru">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, the viewport line, `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">`, `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` …; every `href` and `src` names a file of app/public, or an anchor that exists on its page».
findings.problem: prettier 3.9.9, the first step of the check, writes void elements as `<meta charset="utf-8" />` and `prettier --check` fails on the literal form (measured in the clone: exit 1), so a literal reading cannot hold together with the check. `href="/"` (app/public/404.html as built) and links with `?lang=` name no file literally. The 404 page is also served at nested paths (`/a/b.html` in REQ-108 criterion 5, any path on Vercel), where relative addresses of its style sheets and scripts would miss; criteria 1 and 12 never open it at a nested path.
findings.fix: Name the elements by tag and attributes, say how `/` and a query are read, and cover the 404 page at a nested path (root-relative addresses in criterion 1, or the e2e of criterion 12 opens it at a nested path).

findings.point: а and д (the reach of the text checks: ARCH §17, G8 «б»)
findings.where: «The lint applies to every value of the texts module …, to the visible text and the attribute values … of every page of app/public, and to every string of the intake»; «The order texts: the values of the keys with the prefix `order_` … and the page examples.html».
findings.problem: A visible text written as a literal in a page script, or a sentence that offers ordering outside the order_ keys, passes every check, while ARCH §17 says the lint covers all of Sai's public texts and G8 «б» keeps order texts off production only by the key prefix.
findings.fix: Either a tested rule that every visible text of the pages comes from the texts module, or the e2e of criterion 12 applies the lint to the rendered text of each page in each language; and let the readers of criterion 2 mark any non-order_ pair that offers ordering.

findings.point: а (a condition that cannot be met literally)
findings.where: «each loads by a dynamic import in Node with none of those globals».
findings.problem: `globalThis` cannot be removed in Node, and Node 22 defines `navigator`, `fetch`, `WebSocket`, `performance` and `setTimeout` as globals; the criterion does not say how the test takes them away.
